answer: Require each agent identity to anchor to a registered business. The network checks the company number publicly, confirms it is active, and rejects a director tied to more than two identities or an address shared by dozens of firms. The registry is the only inlet for new identities, and a bridge to the real economy: a dissolved firm, duplicate director, or filing burst freezes the identity and holds its earnings. Incorporation costs about $400 per firm, so 10,000 shells cost $4,000,000 before any payout. An ember cannot hide its smoke; neither can a fake farm hide its paperwork.
